quest.title: Smoldering
quest.description: In order to cure Ineffa's amnesia, everyone searches Natlan for answers...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon — Prelude
chapter.title: The Journey Home

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Um... Do you think Ineffa will like this gift we got her?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Beep-beep.

dialogues.speaker: Yatlan
dialogues.text: See, see? It said "Yes"!

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy
dialogues.text: Are you sure? 'Cause when I asked it who's the better hero, Ixquieh or Lianca, it gave the exact same answer...

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Beep beep beep!

dialogues.speaker: Capac
dialogues.text: Hey, you hear that? That's the answer it gave when I asked who'd win in a fight between Cacucu and Ajaw!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You guys, it's just making random beeps!

dialogues.speaker: Yatlan
dialogues.text: Whoa! Is that... "Tuma{RUBY#[S]Hope}ini" and the flying{RUBY#[D]Paimon} expert?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Uh, beep beep, yes, it's us! Anyway — where's Ineffa?

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy
dialogues.text: Probably out mopping up those mad machines, as usual. There must be a lot of them, 'cause she hardly ever comes back for a rest...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, all by herself? Are we sure that's a good idea after what happened last time...?

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy
dialogues.text: Umm, Ineffa said that since she lost her memories, her... "cognition module's been running more smoothly." And it's... "greatly boosted efficiency in cleaning and tidying tasks"... I think that was it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... So, losing her memories has somehow made her a better fighter?

dialogues.speaker: Capac
dialogues.text: She's awesome! I saw her carrying a whole pile of beaten-up machines in one hand!

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy
dialogues.text: All the grown-ups say that they feel much safer leaving the house now, thanks to her. So we thought it'd be nice to give her a little gift.

dialogues.speaker: Capac
dialogues.text: We've tried giving her flowers and feathers, but it seemed like she didn't like them very much... That got us thinking — maybe robot people don't like the same things as us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-huh... So that's why you made her this flower out of mechanical parts?

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Yeah... we still don't know if she'll like it, though...

dialogues.speaker: Yatlan
dialogues.text: It's okay, Adieta! She'll love this one, I'm sure of it!

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: But... What if she doesn't? This might be my last chance...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Last chance? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Well... Now that all of my mom and dad's other friends from Nod-Krai have left to go home, it's just us left... And they said today, it's our turn to go home too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Already? Wasn't the plan to stick around until Ineffa gets better?

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Dad says everyone back home is expecting us, and he doesn't want us to overstay our welcome here.

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: He thought we should at least make sure Ineffa wasn't getting any worse first, but now that it's been a few days, he says it's time we made a move.

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: To be honest, I can kinda understand. He hasn't been home in so many years. Mom and I can tell that he misses Liyue a lot...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, no wonder... So, what about your mom then? Guessing she's not from Liyue?

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: No, she's from Nod-Krai. She met my dad after he moved there. I was born there, too.

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: He's been there the whole time I was growing up, so... he hasn't been home in at least ten years.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's a long time... No wonder he's getting homesick.

dialogues.speaker: Capac
dialogues.text: Don't worry! We'll write to you and let you know how Ineffa's doing!

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy
dialogues.text: You bet! And once she's all better, we'll bring her to visit you in Liyue!

dialogues.speaker: Yatlan
dialogues.text: Yeah! So don't worry too much about the flower. I'm sure she'll love it, but even if not, you'll have other chances in the future!

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Beep beep!

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Yatlan
dialogues.text: Although... I guess we still need to wait till she gets back. I wonder how much longer she'll be?

dialogues.speaker: Capac
dialogues.text: Who knows... Seems like she takes longer and longer every time she goes out.

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy
dialogues.text: Can't we go take it to her? No, wait... the grown-ups would never let us do that. Way too many of those mad machines out there.

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: What am I gonna do? If she doesn't get back soon, I might run out of time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can deliver it to her for you.

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: *gasp* Really? Thanks, "Tuma{RUBY#[S]Hope}ini"!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Threat eliminated. Scanning for next target...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ineffa!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... Annihilation mode disengaged. Chat mode activated.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chat mode, huh? You'd probably get along well with a Fontainian magician friend of ours... She does "modes" instead of "moods," too.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Good morning. Nice to see you again. What lovely weather we're having.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning. Nice to see you again too. It is lovely, isn't it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, don't you start too! One robot's enough!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: These are some standard greetings I learned recently. Three greetings in a row equals thrice the greetment. Hypothetically speaking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where did you get "greetment" from...? Never mind, you're doing a whole lot better than the last time we met.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Yes. My cognition and language modules are recovering well. I can now sustain fluid conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...But I have still been unable to retrieve the memory containing the code to the cryptex. I will keep trying. Sincere apologies.

choices.text: It's okay, it'll take however long it takes.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Yes. Now that a convenient moment to change the topic has presented itself, what is that object in your hand? A new model of source mechanism?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's a... "flower." Adieta made it for you.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: "Flower"...? Flowers are plant reproductive organs... But I detect no signs of life.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, it's more like a... flower built from mechanical components.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Understood. A flower-shaped machine component... What is its function? Which module is it designed for? Is it compatible with my hardware?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... It doesn't have a "function," it's just for looking at. Y'know... a cute little souvenir.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Cute little souvenir... But if it serves no function, for what purpose was it built?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This conversation just got really deep!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: A cryptex is for sending messages, machines are for performing tasks... What about this flower? What is it for?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I guess... it's to express gratitude.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Gratitude?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. If someone helps you out, you help them back, and if someone gives you a gift, you get them something in return. That's how we show gratitude to other people.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...The Flower-Feather Clan took me in, so I'm neutralizing threats near their territory. Like that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, exactly! You got it! So, it all makes sense now, right?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: But... is this not "tit-for-tat"? I heard Mr. Kinich use this term.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, that's completely different!

choices.text: Ideas like this can take some time to fully grasp.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...I will. Gratitude.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In terms of its purpose... Think of it as a memento of your friendship!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Memento?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: An object that symbolizes an important memory.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's for remembering something or someone by.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Important memory...?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Memento...

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: Here, wear this flower. And this feather, too... There, much better! Gotta look your best for your big journey!
(A flower? Why? It'll only increase the total load...)

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: It's just a flower, it's not that heavy. Just think of it as a little souvenir from me. Something to take with you on the road.
(Souvenir?)

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: That's right — a souvenir. Sometimes, when people have something important to remember, they'll pick an object to use as a reminder of that thing.

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: Even if you end up forgetting everything, this flower will always keep blooming. It could take a thousand times, maybe two thousand... But maybe one day, you'll see the flower bloom — and suddenly, you'll remember the reason for your journey.
(...Shouldn't I stay here and help you?)

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: No. Everyone's on their own path, and they have to walk it alone. Just as your journey is yours, and no one else's.

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: Besides, I have no plan to go to war against him. We both owe each other far more than our mere lives... If either of us actually wanted to claim on that debt, all they'd have to do was ask.

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: If anything... I pity him. In a way, his situation's not so different from yours, but in his case, it's turned him into something neither human nor dragon. The more he chases the sun, the more it blinds him to the creatures who live by its light.

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: You were once... well, "she" was once the enemy of humankind. And Och-Kan doesn't care to distinguish between you and her like Ixquieh and I do. He sees you as the same being.

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: So if you stay behind — and especially if you help me — it'll only stoke the flames of his blind hatred even further.

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: *sigh*... Come on, you have bigger things to worry about than me right now. You have a huge journey ahead of you. That should be your focus.

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: Have faith. This tribe will kneel to no one — they will never be slaves. If they lose their leader, someone else will take up the mantle. Heck, even a child who's barely learned how to walk could do it.

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: Alright, time to go. Some things are destined to be forgotten — don't let it get to you. In a thousand years' time, you'll have a life far, far away from here. So, go...

response.speaker: Unfamiliar Lady
response.text: ...Cross the ocean. Find a new place to belong.
Malfunction who betrayed us all.
...You dare seek a place to belong?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Ineffa! Ineffa! What's wrong?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...Sincere apologies. My cognition module crashed for a moment. It is now fixed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it 'cause you've been fighting for too long? You need to rest. Come on, let's get you back!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Back? ...Back to the Flower-Feather Clan?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, of course... Everything else aside, Adieta and her folks will be leaving soon. Don't you wanna say a proper goodbye?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Is something bothering you?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...Yes. The closer I am to the Flower-Feather Clan, the more erratic my cognition module becomes. Occasionally, unidentified data surfaces from my memory banks.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Ineffa had a similar reaction to this when Xilonen said the name "Lianca"...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Memory data? So... what about that "curse" Xilonen mentioned? Does it not hurt to remember anymore?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: It does. Even now, it still hurts. I have merely switched off the corresponding facial expressions to avoid making other people uncomfortable.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Is that the robot equivalent of "I'm just used to it now"?)

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: But if I do not recall my memories, I cannot complete my task.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... is this why you've been spending so much time out here?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...When memory data surfaces, there is a high probability that my cognition module will crash. This constitutes a safety risk. Therefore, I have been spending time away from the tribe.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (A safety risk... like what happened at the Children of Echoes?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Come back with us. No need to worry about safety risks with us around.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, exactly! Whatever happens, we'll make sure things don't get out of hand!

choices.text: Maybe going back to the tribe will trigger some useful memories.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Assessing relative combat capability... Paimon: approximately one-fifth...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: One fifth? Of what!?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: #{NICKNAME}... Risk mitigated. Strategy accepted.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Great. Let's go!

choices.text: Adieta would really like to say goodbye to you in person.
To start with, will you accept this flower?
Let's see what Xilonen and the others can find out.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: I can't thank you enough for hosting us these past few days... And thanks for agreeing to look after Ineffa. I know it's a lot to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's alright. She'll be in good hands.

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: She never came back... I guess I'll have to leave without saying goodbye...

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: Hey now, you'll see her again! And we have so much to look forward to in Liyue. All those Xiao Lanterns lighting up the sky. You've always wanted to see that!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Adieta, Aamu, Zhuoxin. I am back.

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Huh... Ineffa? ...You brought her back? Thanks so much!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, don't mention it!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Also... gratitude for the flower.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Adieta says a reluctant goodbye to Ineffa...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: What does it feel like... to know where you are returning to?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? That's a strange question... As soon as you're all better, you'll be returning to Nod-Krai!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and we forgot to say — we're actually heading there ourselves soon. Maybe we can travel together!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Nod-Krai... is that home?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Cognition module unable to define "home."

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: All the memory data that has presented itself recently has been related to Natlan. But the merchants tell me that I have "family" waiting for me in Nod-Krai...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: If I do recover my memories, which time period will they be from? And will the post-recovery me be the same "me" that I am now, or someone different?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... That's a deep question...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: What is it that you're afraid of? Are you worried the new you will be so different, you don't even recognize her?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Finding near-synonyms for "mind" and "conflict"... "cognition module"... "split"...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Yes. Once I have been "split"... will it change the way I define "home"?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Huh... Now that's a tough question. A lot of people, and a lot of saurians, spend their whole lives searching for an answer to that.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But if you want my opinion, home is... somewhere you can always return to, wherever that might be.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: No matter how far you fly, there'll always be someone back there waiting for you. No matter how battered and bruised you get, you can always go back there to rest and recover.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I guess you could say, it's somewhere you... belong?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Wherever it is that your memories guide you back to... I'm sure it'll be somewhere you feel safe. Somewhere you feel you belong.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Of course, everyone's situation is different, and I don't know how applicable my experience is in your case. But... consider it a reference point, I guess?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Okay. Recorded under "reference data."

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Heh, and at the end of the day, I mean, who says you can't have more than one home? There's no law against it.

dialogues.speaker: Chimpu
dialogues.text: Squawk...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hmm? Someone's looking for us? Hopefully, this means there's been some progress.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...Don't be afraid to recover your memories. They might contain the answers you're looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Got it.
...Recover your memories?
Malfunction... Have you forgotten why you cast them away to begin with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Citlali! Didn't think it'd be you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Why? Don't you think I'd want to do my part to help {NICKNAME}? ...And anyway, no one's more qualified than the Masters of the Night-Wind when it comes to Natlan's ancient history.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: "Ancient" history? ...Wow, even by Citlali's standards?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...If you think I didn't hear that, you're sorely mistaken. But anyway, back to the matter at hand. I don't know if you noticed, but Kinich's little sidekick has been acting a little strange around Ineffa.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ajaw? Yeah, you can say that again.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: After you parted ways, Kinich put him in timeout for three whole days and nights. Then, he had Ifa send Cacucu to torment him for another night...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Finally, Ajaw got so infuriated with Cacucu's pestering that he lost his cool and let slip a crucial piece of information. Two words: "Sovereign ruler."

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Sovereign ruler? So what, isn't that just how he introduces himself?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It is, and I always assumed it was a load of hot air... But apparently not. Turns out, the title refers to the thirteen dragonlords who ruled Natlan in ancient times.

choices.text: Ooh, I think I've heard of them...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Wait, really? How... It took me forever to figure this out...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Ahem... Anyway, the thirteen sovereign rulers are not ordinary dragons but forms of artificial intelligence created by the Pyro Dragon using secret source technology.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: They had superior intelligence and greater authority than even the ancient dragons themselves. Each ruled over a portion of Natlan's territory.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: But one by one, they disappeared during the war with the heroes... Even most of their names are unknown now, long since buried in the sands of time.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: If we hadn't managed to pry that tidbit out of Ajaw's mouth, I would have had no idea where to even start.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I always thought that little monster's biggest claim to fame was arguing with Cacucu for an entire day... He has quite a history then, huh? Which of the thirteen was he?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Not a clue. So far, he has staunchly refused to reveal which of the sovereign rulers he was... My guess is that he doesn't even remember.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Remember, these rulers were supposed to be powerful forms of artificial intelligence, and Ajaw... Well, it hardly seems like he's still in his prime. I'll bet he's lost most of his memories and power by now.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Lost... memories...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Yet despite that, Ajaw seemed to sense the presence of a fellow sovereign ruler when you were nearby. Specifically, it's the core in your chest he was reacting to.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? Ineffa's a sovereign ruler too!?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Could be. Kinich and Ifa have been keeping a close watch on Ajaw, in case he reveals anything else. But so far, it seems like those two words are all he remembers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Darn... So the trail's gone cold.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Not completely. There's also Lianca and the Flower-Feather Clan, both of which have triggered a response from Ineffa so far. And as it happens, out of the sovereign rulers that I was able to dig up information on, there was one who had a very close relationship with Lianca.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Her name was the Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers, otherwise known as the Eighth Lord. She ruled over what is now the Flower-Feather Clan's territory.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The records claim that she didn't die in the war with humanity, but was executed by her own kind... Her crime being, betrayal of dragonkind by secretly raising a human — Lianca.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? Chasca, did you know this?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Some of it... Our tribe's origin story has Lianca being raised by a dragon, and of the Six Heroes, she had the closest relationship with dragonkind.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: After raising her, her surrogate mother then encouraged her to leave the nest and seek her own path.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: She traveled far and wide, settling disputes between humans and saurians. She didn't pick sides based on past grievances between humanity and dragonkind. She stood up for the weak, protecting them from those more powerful who sought to exploit them...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Gradually, a community of like-minded people and saurians gathered around her, united by their desire for freedom and equality... And that was how the Flower-Feather Clan began.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: But that's as much as the legends say. They never mentioned her dragon mother's name, or what became of her in the end...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Ineffa?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...Oh. Sorry... My cognition module is acting up again. At some point during this conversation, it started behaving very erratically...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: You mentioned that the Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers was "executed"... Might I ask how?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Unfortunately, the humans of that time weren't privy to all the details of dragon affairs... The only records we have are vague references from after the fact.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's very possible that this is mere speculation or complete fabrication, so don't give too much weight to it. But for what it's worth — it's said that a curse was placed on the priestess by one of the other rulers:

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: "If she truly harbors pro-human sentiment... then for every ounce of goodwill she feels, may her mind be flooded with pain of immeasurable proportions."

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...In the savage conflict and chaos that followed, the priestess's mind was ultimately destroyed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Geez, what a bizarre method of execution... Definitely sounds like the history writers used some artistic license there.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Are you okay?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: I'm fine... This didn't seem to trigger any erratic behavior. So, do you think that my origins have something to do with this sovereign ruler?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hmm, interesting... Well, it's hard to say what, if any, direct connection you have to the Eighth Lord. But since the name "Lianca" seems to ring a bell for you, why don't you look into it yourself?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #I brought some woven scrolls with me that might be useful. Have a look if you're interested. Here, take them, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You mean me...?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: (...Don't say anything. In a moment I'm going to leave. I need you to join me, discreetly.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Am I... hearing your thoughts?)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: (It's just a little spell based on our prior experience. I'll explain everything shortly when you catch up with me.)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...Well, I need to get going now. If I find out anything more, I'll keep you updated.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Gratitude. Goodbye.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bye, Citlali!

choices.text: Hmm, don't think I've heard much about them...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hehe, of course you haven't. Even I spent forever figuring it out!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #Hello, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Xilonen? What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Well, Citlali hasn't told you everything. There's another sovereign ruler that Ineffa might be connected to, not just the one from the Flower-Feather Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: All trace of this other sovereign ruler was lost after the war. The records claim that in their final battle, they fought against Ixquieh... and Lianca.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What!? Why didn't you say anything?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: It was my idea. I suggested we bring up the dragon mother first and see how Ineffa responds. And, well... Citlali has debriefed me on how it went.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Apparently, she barely reacted — despite a very strong reaction to the name "Lianca"... To me, that says we need to tread very carefully when probing her about the Eleventh Lord.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about the Eleventh Lord...?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: She's the one who went missing after the war. Said to be the proudest of all the sovereign rulers — and the most hostile towards humanity.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: When the Pyro Dragon fell, she couldn't accept that dragonkind had been defeated. She sank into despair and insanity...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But the rest is lost to history. There's no way to find out what became of her, or even what her name was.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Remember, though — in essence, these sovereign rulers weren't physical entities, but pure intelligence, built with secret source technology.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I mean, who knows what happens when a manufactured mind goes mad? Maybe she lost her power and memories... maybe she split into different personalities.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you saying what I think you're saying?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The point is, if Ineffa really does originate from the Eleventh Lord, then we need to...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: What, have her taken out? Because of some baseless speculation? How would that be any different from what they did to Lianca's mother?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Chasca? Wh—What, uh, brings you here...?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Anyone with a brain could see you were up to something back there... Unless it's a Paimon-brain. Or a robot-brain.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #...Okay, you got us. Actually, we never intended to cut you out of this, it's just that Citlali's spell only works on {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But Chasca, I'm telling you — we have legitimate concerns here. This is not baseless speculation.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Ever since Ineffa set sail for Natlan, the secret source automatons have been getting increasingly aggressive... It's as if they're drawn to each other.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: ...Ineffa could well be the Eleventh Lord herself. And if so, then the moment she recovers her memory, all of us — all of humanity — will instantly become her enemy.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I've been keeping an eye on her movements at the Flower-Feather Clan. Whatever she was in the past, and whoever she becomes in the future, I trust who she is today.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Even if the past and future Ineffa are a completely different person from who she is now?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Heh... If you're suggesting that there's a volatile force within her, threatening to rise up and take over at any given moment... That makes two of us.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But no one ever gave up on me. Not momma bird, not Chuychu, not my dad... So what right do I have to give up on her?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: If Lianca was here... I have every confidence that she'd say the same.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Besides, even if the Eleventh Lord rises again and declares all of us her enemy, the solution is simple: We defeat her. The heroes managed it, so there's no reason we can't too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Especially with Tumaini on the team.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Fine, fine. I had a feeling this might be your reaction.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Look, I get it — you're only acting like the villain here to make us realize how serious the situation is. You know how I know that? Because when I was a kid, and they brought me to you for treatment, you didn't give up on me either.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yeah, well, playing the villain is a force of habit for old Granny by this point... Just know you've been warned, alright? Watch out for any new developments, and make sure you know where she is at all times...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Haha, that really sounded like a granny talking to a rebellious teen...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Hey! The spell hasn't worn off yet, you know!)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ahem... Anyway, now that we're all caught up, you should get back on Ineffa watch, and we should get back to investigating...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Help, someone...! Oh... Chasca? What are you all doing here? And when did Xilonen show up?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Paimon? You were supposed to stay with Ineffa...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right, Ineffa! Something weird happened. She got halfway through those woven scrolls, and then flew off all of a sudden! Paimon tried to stop her, but she wouldn't come back!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Did something trigger a new memory? This doesn't make any sense... She barely responded when we were chatting. What could it be?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No idea... But it must be something important, 'cause she sure looked like she was in a hurry... Also, she said... "Annihilation mode activated"!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: ...! Okay, Chasca, you're our eye in the sky — find out where she's gone. We'll inform everyone else, tell them to be on high alert.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Roger that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm coming with you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, don't you wanna discuss this first— Hey, wait up!

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: Ah... Aaah!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Target acquired. Activating annihilation mode.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Whoa, are these all secret source automatons?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's take them out!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...Okay!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Threat eliminated. Annihilation mode disengaged.

dialogues.speaker: Gulebu
dialogues.text: Ugh! Boss, what do we do now?

dialogues.speaker: Fajeyi
dialogues.text: We've tried the same thing several times now, and it isn't working. We can't keep waiting around for her to leave the settlement...
...Well, well. An ancient relic from Natlan's dragon civilization? Hmph...
If you want to play with fire, then be my guest. But there is an unpredictable variable you need to watch out for...

dialogues.speaker: Velimiru
dialogues.text: ...Let's fall back. This isn't worth the risk.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Aamu, Adieta! Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: I—I'm fine, but mom's hurt...

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: I'll be okay, I just hurt my ankle... Ineffa got here just in time...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Why would they do this? Ugh... Argh! Why!!!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: No one could have known the automatons would ambush you here. Don't blame yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Ineffa, how did you know to come here? Did you sense that they were in danger?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Yes, I... heard the secret source automatons... talking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh, well that's interesting...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Even now, I still hear them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Paimon doesn't hear anything!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Hypothesis: language module requires translation functionality... Please wait...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Ineffa dismantles the automatons...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Finished. Please try again.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: That was quick... How come you're so familiar with their architecture?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I have... seen them many times before. At least, I think so.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hmm. More random memory data, I guess...

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: ...Reconnecting...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! It's actually talking!

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Hey! What do you think you're playing at? Why did you attack us!?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: ...Under... Fatui... control... they... made us... attack...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Fatui!?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: How is that possible? The Captain's soldiers certainly aren't capable of this, and besides — we know everything they're up to... Has another Fatui regiment infiltrated Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: ...Fatui... invaded... territory... haywire...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, why's it getting so choppy? Bad signal, maybe?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Hypothesis: Distance to signal source increasing, transmission compromised. Combining these words with what I have heard so far, I believe the full message should be:

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: "The Fatui invaded my territory, so the automatons went haywire."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... So all the recent automaton attacks — the Fatui were behind it all along?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Stole... privileges... control...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: "They stole my privileges and took control of the automatons."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So... who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Mirror of the Dawning Morn... detected... sending... request... restore...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: "Mirror of the Dawning Morn detected nearby. Now sending request for Mirror of the Dawning Morn to restore my privileges."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Mirror of the Dawning Morn"? Who or what is that?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Hypothesis: This appears to refer to me... or more specifically, to my core.

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Mirror of the Dawning Morn... return... core...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I think... she wants me to go with her to return the core. So she can repair the damage done by the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you mean... she knows you?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Yes. Before the translation began, she referred to me by a different name: "Eleventh Lord."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So Ineffa is the missing sovereign ruler who fought against Lianca?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? So... Ineffa is the eleventh sovereign ruler!?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hold on... This automaton just attacked us moments ago. We shouldn't trust everything it says.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You say Ineffa is the Eleventh Lord. What proof do you have?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: ...Return... Eighth Lord's... territory... restore... memory...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ineffa? Wh—What did she say?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: She said, return to the Eighth Lord's territory, and I can restore all of my memory data.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Eighth Lord... Lianca's mother's territory? What does the Eleventh Lord have to do with that?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: ...Split... exiled... reborn...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, this is getting weirder by the second... What did she say this time?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Excessive signal interference... Unable to translate.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: #The signal should improve as we get closer to her territory. {NICKNAME}, Chasca, shall we proceed?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Wait! ...Um... You should think this through carefully...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: I... may know a thing or two about the Fatui regiment that entered Natlan recently. They're kind of a special ops team... definitely not your average soldiers.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: They've been showing up everywhere, hungrily searching for secret knowledge about all kinds of ancient civilizations... they say they're trying to make some sort of... "inference."

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: The leader of this regiment is a harbinger based in Nod-Krai... known as "Marionette."

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Marionette? ...How exactly do you know all this?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: I, uh... heard bits and pieces at the market in Nasha Town. But I figured they were just rumors. Didn't realize it was true...

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: Is that right? How come I'm only hearing about this now?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... I was so preoccupied with getting ready for the journey, and like I said, I thought they were just rumors anyway... Didn't wanna worry you...

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: So these Fatui are soldiers, huh? Who's stronger, them or Ineffa?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Ineffa, of course! Haha... But still... maybe you should tread carefully here? Ineffa's already had to rescue us so many times now, I... I'd be mortified if anything happened to you.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...You're right. First things first, Aamu's injured — we should take her back to the tribe and get her checked out. And as for this "Eleventh Lord" business... We need to discuss this with the others before deciding how to proceed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (An Eleventh Lord with her memories back will probably see humanity as her enemy... Xilonen and Citlali's worst fears might be coming true. We need to tell them.)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Look, I know the news about the Eighth Lord and Marionette is very concerning... But we should probably come up with a plan before checking things out.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Understood. Destination canceled.

choices.text: Don't lose hope. This is still a big breakthrough.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Yes. New destination: Flower-Feather Clan.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Ineffa, could you check that the coast is clear? I'm gonna patch up Aamu, then head out.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Understood. Commencing task.

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: ...Adieta, I need you to go keep mom company while the doctor takes a look at her. Dad has some things to take care of, so I'll be staying out here a while longer...

response.speaker: Adieta
response.text: You're not coming back with us? Why not?

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: Dad's gotta pack up the luggage and make sure all our goods are safe! Don't forget, they're our ticket to a great new life in Liyue!

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: Don't worry, Dad will be back very soon... I'm sorry girls, I promise it's going to be okay.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I'll get help as quickly as I can. If anything happens, save yourselves first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh? Why'd it stop moving? Has it malfunctioned on us?

response.speaker: Little Robot
response.text: Liyue... merchant...

response.speaker: Little Robot
response.text: His portrait... at Fatui... stronghold...

choices.text: We'll follow up on all this soon. It won't be long.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...You're saying Zhuoxin might be a Fatui spy? And he's staying behind as their eyes on the ground?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But... Should we really leave Ineffa here too? Not that I don't trust her, it's just... are you sure you'll be okay keeping an eye on her by yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll be fine.

choices.text: If we get anything more out of the automatons...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...You're not wrong. We need all the intel we can get on Marionette and the Fatui — as far as I'm concerned, they're a bigger threat than any sovereign ruler.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Still, even with your abilities, be sure to stay on your guard. And not just because of the Fatui and the Eleventh Lord... it's that automaton, too. I'm still not convinced we can trust it.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Why the sudden request for assistance from the Eighth Lord's territory? Are we supposed to believe that Lianca's mother survived? Surely, there'd be at least some mention of that in the tribal legends... I don't know, something just doesn't add up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Chasca! Aamu's ready to go!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: That's my cue... I'll be back with the others as soon as I've gotten Aamu and Adieta to safety. If you have to leave the area for any reason... be sure to leave a trail.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I will.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...He's on the move! So much for keeping the goods safe... Do we think he's going to meet someone?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Should we tail him? He won't know he's being followed — this could be our chance to get our hands on some really useful intel! Either about the sovereign rulers or this "Marionette" person...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, shall I follow him?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Let's do it. Make sure you leave a trail, so we can be traced.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Got it.

choices.text: She's the only one who can make sense of it.

talks.objective: Keep your distance and follow Zhuoxin
Keep your distance and follow Zhuoxin

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now, why would someone dig a random tunnel in the middle of nowhere? Unless... it's the entrance to one of the sovereign rulers' territories?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Territory... sealed by Lianca... This was... once one of... the secondary access tunnels...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, that was pretty clear this time. What's changed?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: ...Getting closer... increased activity in language module...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean by "sealed"?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: ...Li... Och... finding...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You're breaking up again... Looks like the signal's still pretty choppy.

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: ...Lianca sealed... territory... stop Och-Kan... finding it...

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Later... Fatui... weak point... broke in...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like those Fatui have made this their stronghold... Well, this is probably a good point to stop and wait for reinforcements.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you think? Ineffa... Oh no! What's she doing!? She charged right in!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: *sigh* I take my eyes off her for two seconds, and now this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, are we going after her? Or waiting here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...We're going after her.

choices.text: I promised to watch over her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then... But let's be careful!

dialogues.speaker: Capac
dialogues.text: All the grown-ups I know who've been to Liyue say it's a really beautiful place! They have loads of cool toys there too, right?

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Umm... I only know what my dad's told me. He said there's a toy seller at Chihu Rock...

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy
dialogues.text: Sounds awesome...

dialogues.speaker: Yatlan
dialogues.text: Once you get there, you have to write to us and tell us all about it!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Would a machine created by dragons really betray its own kind? Hmm... She seemed to approve of the path her daughter took — but what about her? What path did she take?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: None of the legends of Lianca say anything about her dragon mother defecting to humanity and fighting against dragonkind... Sounds like speculation to me. Maybe the other sovereign rulers just didn't trust her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So mean! Hmm... Do you think it's possible that Lianca found a way to secretly save the priestess of... uhh, flower-feather... something?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (...Now's your chance. Slip away quietly while they've got their heads buried in those woven scrolls. Meet me at the other side of the settlement.)
